title: Rotating beams
subtitle: Build a readable rotating beams with a reachable response and a useful recovery.
summary: Two or more beam arms rotate around a source.
overview: Two or more beam arms rotate around a source, dividing the arena into moving sectors whose spacing defines a continuous navigation rhythm.
learning: Tune the signal, commitment, geometry, response, and recovery of a rotating beams as one rule.

demo.title: Test the rotating beams
phaseDescriptions: Show arm count, rotation direction, and safe sector size before damage begins; all active arms should share an understandable pivot.
The player follows a safe sector, crosses one arm at a controlled moment, or changes radius to alter the required movement speed.
The rotating arms visibly stall and fade before direction or arm count can change, giving the player a clean rhythm break.

steps.title: Can the player read the complete rule?
steps.body: Show arm count, rotation direction, and safe sector size before damage begins; all active arms should share an understandable pivot.

steps.title: Is the intended response reachable?
steps.body: The player follows a safe sector, crosses one arm at a controlled moment, or changes radius to alter the required movement speed.

steps.title: Does recovery create a useful outcome?
steps.body: The rotating arms visibly stall and fade before direction or arm count can change, giving the player a clean rhythm break.

mistakes.title: Too many wide arms erase the safe sector and reduce the mechanic to mandatory invulnerability frames
mistakes.body: Too many wide arms erase the safe sector and reduce the mechanic to mandatory invulnerability frames.

mistakes.title: The cue and active geometry disagree
mistakes.body: If the visible rotating beams cue promises a different area or timing, the player cannot carry the learned rule into the next cycle.

designNotes.title: Tune the complete rule
designNotes.body: Coordinate arm count, angular speed, width, radius, and duration; verify that camera motion does not disguise the world-space rotation.

designNotes.title: Escalate one variable at a time
designNotes.body: Change direction or arm count only at signaled breaks, giving the player time to adopt the new rhythm.

designNotes.title: Prove the recovery
designNotes.body: The rotating arms visibly stall and fade before direction or arm count can change, giving the player a clean rhythm break.

story.title: What the mechanic communicates
story.body: Two or more beam arms rotate around a source, dividing the arena into moving sectors whose spacing defines a continuous navigation rhythm. The encounter uses that rule as a short promise: a visible signal, a committed action, and a result the player can verify.

adaptation.title: Adapt it to the player verbs
adaptation.body: The player follows a safe sector, crosses one arm at a controlled moment, or changes radius to alter the required movement speed. Coordinate arm count, angular speed, width, radius, and duration; verify that camera motion does not disguise the world-space rotation.

distinction.title: Keep the mechanic distinct
distinction.body: Too many wide arms erase the safe sector and reduce the mechanic to mandatory invulnerability frames. Do not hide that distinction behind extra effects or tracking that the announced rule does not contain.

lensNotes.body: The signal must reveal the relevant timing and geometry before commitment.
After commitment, the rule stops changing in ways the signal did not announce.
The complete player extent and the active region determine whether the route is real.
The response uses an ordinary supported verb and produces an observable result.

examples.body: Absolute Radiance demonstrates rotating beams in a 2D encounter. Show arm count, rotation direction, and safe sector size before damage begins; all active arms should share an understandable pivot.
Phrike demonstrates rotating beams in a 3D encounter. The player follows a safe sector, crosses one arm at a controlled moment, or changes radius to alter the required movement speed.

Ziva the Engineer demonstrates rotating beams in a 3D encounter. Coordinate arm count, angular speed, width, radius, and duration; verify that camera motion does not disguise the world-space rotation.
